appraisal_events.evidence: Mon père haussait les épaules et il examinait le baromètre...ma mère, évitant de faire du bruit pour ne pas le troubler, le regardait avec un respect attendri, mais pas trop fixement pour ne pas chercher à percer le mystère de ses supériorités...la concession qu'elle faisait à ma tristesse...agaçait mon père qui trouvait ces rites absurdes.
appraisal_events.explanation: The father's authority goes unquestioned in the household: he silently dismisses the grandmother's parenting advice, and the mother curbs her own goodnight tenderness so as not to irritate him, though the narrator's phrase 'the mystery of his superiorities' lightly mocks this unexamined household reverence.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Bathilde ! viens donc empêcher ton mari de boire du cognac ! »...Ce supplice que lui infligeait ma grand'tante, le spectacle des vaines prières de ma grand'mère et de sa faiblesse, vaincue d'avance...elles me causaient alors une telle horreur, que j'aurais aimé battre ma grand'tante.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator condemns the great-aunt's game of summoning the grandmother to fail at stopping the grandfather's cognac, naming it a torment he found so horrifying he wanted to strike her.

appraisal_events.evidence: M. Swann,...quelquefois pour dîner en voisin (plus rarement depuis qu'il avait fait ce mauvais mariage, parce que mes parents ne voulaient pas recevoir sa femme).
appraisal_events.explanation: Swann's visits become rarer because his 'bad marriage' means the family will not receive his wife, a clear local social discredit tied to that marriage.

status_effects.explanation: His word goes unchallenged and his moods are carefully managed by the rest of the household, though the narrator's irony about the 'mystery of his superiorities' tempers the elevation.
Her argument for toughening the child outdoors is not engaged with, only shrugged off, as the father turns to the barometer instead.
She must limit her own affectionate goodnight gesture to avoid irritating her husband, subordinating her tenderness to his preferences.
The narrator explicitly frames her as a tormentor whose game causes him horror, a strongly negative local verdict.
She is described as defeated in advance, pleading in vain against her husband's drinking, powerless despite her tenderness.
His standing with the family is diminished because his marriage is treated as socially unacceptable, curtailing his visits.

ambiguities: The narrator's account of the father's unquestioned household authority (E1) carries a light retrospective irony ('the mystery of his superiorities'), so the elevation is not read as fully endorsed.
